title: How to read companies for pellet / CBG sales

sources.title: EY — CCTS: Accelerating the path to decarbonization (2026)
EY — Carbon pricing meets raw materials: CBAM’s impact on Indian industries (2026)
CCTS + CBAM Targeting Summary v7 (internal workbook)

headline: India’s carbon market (CCTS) and Europe’s border carbon tax (CBAM) push factories to cut intensity. Many will need cleaner fuels or a decarbonization partner — not just carbon credits.
takeaways: Start with the company story: Net Zero plans, ESG spend, biomass already in use, and whether they sell to Europe.
Green credits in BRSR are often Nil. Do not lead with “we sell carbon credits.” Lead with reliable fuel that cuts coal use.
Steel and aluminium face the strongest Europe pressure. Cement and pulp & paper are natural biomass buyers.
The targeting workbook has researched ESG / carbon profiles for 113 company groups — use those first.
Price vs coal matters, but missed biomass supply has already hurt some emitters’ targets. Continuity wins deals.

sectors.cctsFocus: Steel plants are under draft carbon intensity targets. Falling short can mean buying expensive carbon certificates later.
sectors.cbamFocus: Steel is India’s biggest CBAM risk. Selling to Europe gets harder if plant carbon intensity stays high.
levers: Try gas or hydrogen in ironmaking (longer term)
Mix biomass or biochar into captive power and some iron processes
sectors.partnerAngle: Best near-term offer: steady pellets or briquettes for captive power, priced against coal. Europe-facing mills also care about proof of lower intensity.

sectors.cctsFocus: Smelters and refineries already have final carbon targets. Missing them means certificate costs.
sectors.cbamFocus: Aluminium metal sold to Europe faces CBAM. Coal power at the plant makes the carbon number look worse.
sectors.partnerAngle: Strong pellet/briquette fit for captive power. Long-term supply deals matter as much as price.

sectors.cctsFocus: Cement (including grinding) has final targets. Alternative fuels are a normal lever.
sectors.cbamFocus: Cement/clinker exports to Europe can face CBAM. India volumes are smaller than steel.
sectors.partnerAngle: Pitch consistent kiln fuel quality and reliable plant deliveries.

sectors.cctsFocus: Final targets. Power cost and renewable PPAs matter more than biomass for many sites.
sectors.cbamFocus: Mostly outside core CBAM metal/cement lists.
levers: Fuel switch where coal boilers exist
sectors.partnerAngle: Look for sites with coal boilers; otherwise treat as a longer-cycle partner.

sectors.cctsFocus: Final targets. Biomass for steam is a core lever.
sectors.partnerAngle: Natural buyer of pellets/briquettes for boilers — supply continuity is critical.

sectors.cctsFocus: Final targets from 2026-27. Cleaner heat and renewable power help compliance.
sectors.partnerAngle: Often price-sensitive mid-size buyers; carbon rules still create pull for cleaner heat.

sectors.cctsFocus: Final targets. Decarbonization leans on electrification, alternate fuels, and CCUS.
sectors.cbamFocus: Refined products mostly outside CBAM (hydrogen can be an exception).
sectors.partnerAngle: Harder agro-pellet fit; CBG or gas partnerships may be more relevant.
Selective thermal substitution — longer sales cycle.
